'''James Desmond Caldwell McConnell''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (1930 – 2026) was a mineralogist, who was a lecturer in the [[University of Cambridge]] (1955 – 1982), director of the rock physics laboratory at [[SLB|Schlumberger Cambridge Research]] (1983 – 1986), and then Professor of the Physics and Chemistry of Minerals at the [[University of Oxford]], from 1986 to 1995. He was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1987.<ref name=Obit>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2026/feb/19/desmond-mcconnell-obituary|title=Desmond McConnell obituary|first=Deirdre|last=Simmen McConnell|date=19 February 2026|newspaper=Guardian|access-date=10 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/james-mcconnell-11917/|title=Professor James McConnell FRS|via=Royal Society|access-date=10 September 2026}}</ref>

==Early life==
McConnell was born in Lisburn, Northern Ireland in 1930, the eldest son of Samuel McConnell, primary school teacher, and Cathleen (nee Coulter), a secretary. He studied geology at Queen's, Belfast, before moving to Cambridge in 1952 to start a PhD.<ref name=Obit/>

In Cambridge, he was a founding fellow of [[Churchill College, Cambridge|Churchill College]], and lecturer in the department of Earth Sciences from 1962 to 1982.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chu.cam.ac.uk/obituaries/professor-desmond-mcconnell/|title=Professor Desmond McConnell FRS|via=Churchill College|access-date=10 September 2026}}</ref> In 1986, McConnell moved the [[University of Oxford]] to take up the Professorship of Physics and Chemistry of Minerals in the [[Department of Earth Sciences, University of Oxford|Department of Geology and Mineralogy]]. He also took up a Professorial Fellowship at [[St Hugh's College, Oxford]] at the same time. McConnell retired from both roles in 1995, and was later elected an Honorary Fellow at St Hugh's.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.st-hughs.ox.ac.uk/desmond-mcconnell/|title=St Hugh’s Honorary Fellow, Desmond McConnell, has passed away|via=St Hugh's College|access-date=10 September 2026}}</ref>

==Research career==
McConnell's research interests focussed on the area of the structures of crystalline materials. During his PhD work, he used X-ray techniques to investigate the crystal structures of silicate minerals that contained water.<ref>{{Cite journal
| last = McConnell
| first = J.D.C.
| year = 1954
| title = The hydrated calcium silicates riversideite, tobermorite and plombierite
| journal = Mineralogical Magazine
| volume = 30
| issue = 224
| pages = 293–305
| doi = 10.1180/minmag.1954.030.224.02
| bibcode = 1954MinM...30..293M
| s2cid = 94792892
}}</ref> Later, he developed theories to explain the general features of complex crystalline silicate minerals, in particular those that form solid solutions.<ref>{{cite journal|last=McConnell|first=J. D. C.|title=Incommensurate Structures [and Discussion]|journal=Philosophical Transactions: Physical Sciences and Engineering|volume=334|year=1991|pages=425–37|via=STOR|url= http://www.jstor.org/stable/53736}}</ref>

In 1969, McConnell got the chance to work on some [[Moon|Lunar]] rock samples, collected during the [[Apollo 11]] mission. [[Stuart Olof Agrell|Stuart Agrell]], a colleague in Cambridge, as the only non-US principal investigator working on the [[petrology]] of the collected samples, brought some samples to the UK in September 1969.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/nostalgia/london-underground-incredible-pictures-show-24529260|title=Incredible pictures show scientist carrying bag of moondust on the Tube|first=Martin|last=Elvery|date=24 July 2022|website=MyLondon}}</ref> The results of their analyses were published early the next year.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=S. O.|last1=Agrell|first2=J. H.|last2=Scoon|first3=I. D.|last3=Muir|first4=J. V. P.|last4=Long|first5=J. D. C.|last5=McConnell|first6=A.|last6=Peckett|title=Mineralogy and Petrology of Some Lunar Samples|journal=Science|volume=167|pages=583-586|year=1970|doi=10.1126/science.167.3918.583}}</ref>

From 1983 to 1986, McConnell was the director of the rock physics laboratory at the Schlumberger Cambridge research centre. This gave him an opportunity to work on experimental and theoretical investigations on the properties of some industrially-important minerals, including clays and gypsum.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Hall|first1=PL|last2=Astill|first2=DM|last3=McConnell|first3=JDC|title=Thermodynamic and structural aspects of the dehydration of smectites in sedimentary rocks|journal=Clay Minerals|year=1986|volume=21|pages=633-648|doi=10.1180/claymin.1986.021.4.13}}</ref>
